checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas cap enforced for ALL transaction types (legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-4844)?
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-0010, Trust Boundaries: tb-001, tb-003, Invariant: INV-010 (SG-003, EIP-7825)

phase1.summary: EIP-7825 per-transaction gas cap enforcement is a purely execution-layer (EL) feature. Prysm is a consensus/beacon-chain client written in Go. The EVM execution engine — including transaction validation, gas accounting, and per-transaction gas cap enforcement — is the responsibility of the paired execution client (e.g., go-ethereum/geth). Prysm does not contain any EVM execution code, transaction gas validation logic, or precompile implementations.
phase1.abstract_interpretation: Searched Prysm codebase for: 'GasCap', 'gas cap', 'gasLimit', 'ValidateTransaction', 'EIP-7825', '16777217', '16777216'. No relevant execution-layer gas cap enforcement code was found. The value 16777217 appears only in test files related to slot/epoch indexing (beacon chain concepts), unrelated to EVM gas limits.

phase2.summary: No symbolic execution paths possible — no EVM execution code exists in Prysm target repository.
phase2.symbolic_execution: Prysm delegates all transaction execution to the execution client via Engine API (NewPayload/ForkchoiceUpdated). The beacon chain validates block structure, attestations, and state transitions but does not execute EVM transactions directly. No code path for per-transaction gas cap validation exists in this codebase.

phase2_5.summary: Component boundary analysis confirms out-of-scope classification.
phase2_5.component_analysis: EIP-7825 gas cap enforcement must be checked in the execution client (go-ethereum, besu, nethermind, erigon). Prysm is not an execution client. Audit scope for this checklist item does not match the target repository (OffchainLabs/prysm, commit 238d5c07df).

phase3.summary: Formal proof of out-of-scope: The implementation domain for EIP-7825 gas cap enforcement is the EVM execution layer. Prysm does not implement EVM execution.
phase3.invariant_proving: The property INV-010 requires existence of per-transaction gas validation code. No such code exists in the Prysm codebase. The property cannot be verified or falsified against this codebase.

phase3_5.rationale: This checklist item targets EVM execution-layer gas cap enforcement (EIP-7825). The Prysm codebase is a consensus-layer client that does not implement EVM execution, transaction gas validation, or precompile logic. The implementation of EIP-7825 resides in execution clients such as go-ethereum. This item is definitively out of scope for the Prysm target repository.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is multiplication_complexity >= 16 for all ModExp inputs?
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-0011, Trust Boundary: tb-005, Invariant: INV-001 (SG-001, EIP-7883)

phase1.summary: EIP-7883 ModExp gas pricing is a purely execution-layer (EL) precompile feature. The ModExp precompile (address 0x05) and its gas calculation — including multiplication_complexity — are implemented in EVM execution clients, not in consensus clients. Prysm does not contain precompile code.
phase1.abstract_interpretation: Searched Prysm codebase for: 'ModExp', 'modexp', 'multiplication_complexity', 'precompile', 'EIP-7883', '7883'. No ModExp precompile implementation or gas calculation code was found. The word 'precompile' appears only in C++ build toolchain configuration files and Bazel build scripts, unrelated to EVM precompiles.

phase2.summary: No symbolic execution paths possible for ModExp gas calculation — Prysm is a consensus client with no EVM precompile code.
phase2.symbolic_execution: The ModExp precompile (EIP-7883) gas formula involves: iteration_count, multiplication_complexity, and adjusted_exponent_length. None of these concepts exist in the Prysm codebase. Prysm relies on the execution client (via Engine API) to execute all EVM transactions including precompile calls.

phase2_5.summary: Out-of-scope confirmed. ModExp precompile is an execution layer concern.
phase2_5.component_analysis: EIP-7883 modifies the gas calculation for the BigModExp precompile (EIP-198). This is implemented in EVM execution clients. The target repository (Prysm) has no EVM execution stack.

phase3.summary: Formal proof of out-of-scope: ModExp gas pricing belongs to the execution layer. Prysm is a consensus-layer client.
phase3.invariant_proving: The property INV-001 requires a multiplication_complexity computation function. No such function exists in Prysm. The property cannot be evaluated against this codebase.

phase3_5.rationale: This checklist item targets the ModExp precompile gas calculation (EIP-7883), specifically whether multiplication_complexity >= 16 is enforced. The Prysm codebase is a consensus-layer client with no EVM execution code. ModExp precompile implementation resides in execution clients (e.g., go-ethereum). This item is definitively out of scope for Prysm.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is multiplication_complexity exactly 16 when max(base_length, modulus_length) <= 32?
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-0012, Trust Boundary: tb-005, Invariant: INV-002 (SG-001, EIP-7883)

phase1.summary: This check tests INV-002: multiplication_complexity == 16 when max(base_length, modulus_length) <= 32 (the small-operand case of EIP-7883). This is an EVM precompile gas formula boundary condition. Prysm has no EVM execution code.
phase1.abstract_interpretation: Searched for 'ModExp', 'multiplication_complexity', '16', base_length/modulus_length calculations. No relevant code exists in Prysm. The constant 16 appears in Prysm only in beacon chain contexts (slots per epoch, validator set sizes), not in EVM gas calculations.

phase2.summary: No symbolic execution paths for ModExp boundary condition — Prysm is a consensus client.
phase2.symbolic_execution: The boundary condition max(base_length, modulus_length) <= 32 → complexity = 16 is specific to EIP-7883's modification of the BigModExp gas formula. This belongs entirely to the execution layer. No relevant code paths exist in Prysm.

phase2_5.component_analysis: Same as CHK-0011: EIP-7883 is an execution-layer EIP modifying precompile gas calculations. Prysm is a consensus-layer client.

phase3.summary: Property INV-002 cannot be evaluated against Prysm — no ModExp implementation exists.
phase3.invariant_proving: The small-operand case boundary condition (complexity == 16 when max_length <= 32) requires a ModExp gas calculation function. Prysm has none. Property is out of scope.

phase3_5.rationale: This item checks a specific boundary condition in EIP-7883's ModExp gas formula (small operand case). Prysm is a consensus client with no EVM execution or precompile code. Out of scope for Prysm.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is multiplication_complexity = 2 * ceil(max_length/8)^2 for large operands?
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-0013, Trust Boundary: tb-005, Invariant: INV-003 (SG-001, EIP-7883)

phase1.summary: This check tests INV-003: multiplication_complexity = 2 * ceil(max_length/8)^2 for the large-operand case of EIP-7883. This formula uses ceiling division (not floor), which is a critical correctness point. However, this is an EVM precompile gas formula — implemented in execution clients, not Prysm.
phase1.abstract_interpretation: Searched for ceil division patterns, ModExp formula, max_length calculations. No relevant code exists in Prysm. The formula 2 * ceil(x/8)^2 is specific to EIP-7883's BigModExp precompile gas calculation. This is an execution-layer concern.

phase2.summary: No code paths for ceiling-based multiplication complexity formula in Prysm.
phase2.symbolic_execution: The large-operand formula (ceil division) is the most security-critical part of EIP-7883 — a floor instead of ceiling division would undercharge gas, enabling DoS. However, this vulnerability, if it exists, would be in execution clients (go-ethereum, besu, etc.), not in Prysm.
attack_paths_explored: Floor vs ceiling division — could produce complexity < 2*(ceil(x/8))^2 — not applicable to Prysm
Non-multiples of 8 boundary cases (33, 34, 39, 41...) — not applicable to Prysm

phase2_5.summary: Out-of-scope confirmed. Critical formula verification belongs to execution clients.
phase2_5.component_analysis: Even though this is Critical severity and involves a formula correctness check (floor vs ceiling), the entire implementation domain is execution-layer. Prysm has no ModExp code to audit.

phase3.summary: Property INV-003 cannot be evaluated — no ModExp gas formula exists in Prysm.
phase3.invariant_proving: The large-operand multiplication_complexity formula is an execution-layer invariant. No relevant code in Prysm to prove or disprove this property against.

phase3_5.rationale: This Critical severity item checks the large-operand ModExp gas formula (ceiling division correctness in EIP-7883). Despite its severity, this is purely an execution-layer concern. Prysm is a consensus client with no EVM execution code. The formula correctness check must be performed against execution clients (go-ethereum, besu, etc.). Out of scope for OffchainLabs/prysm.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is iteration_count >= 1 for all non-trivial ModExp inputs?
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-0014, Trust Boundary: tb-005, Invariant: INV-001 (SG-002, EIP-7883)

phase1.summary: This check tests INV-001: iteration_count >= 1 always (enforced via max(calculated_value, 1) clamp) for the ModExp precompile (EIP-7883). Zero-cost execution via iteration_count=0 would be a DoS vector. This is an execution-layer precompile concern; Prysm has no ModExp implementation.
phase1.abstract_interpretation: Searched for 'iteration_count', 'modexp', 'adjusted_exponent_length', 'exponent_length'. No relevant code exists in Prysm. The max(calculated_value, 1) clamp pattern for iteration_count is specific to EIP-7883's gas formula and is implemented in execution clients.

phase2.summary: No zero-cost execution path analysis possible — no ModExp code in Prysm.
phase2.symbolic_execution: The zero-cost execution vulnerability would manifest if: exponent=0, exponent_length > 0, and the code fails to apply max(.,1) clamp. This is a known attack pattern against underpriced precompiles. However, in Prysm, no such code path exists. The execution client is responsible for computing iteration_count with the appropriate clamp.
attack_paths_explored: Zero exponent with non-zero exponent_length producing iteration_count=0 — not applicable to Prysm
max(.,1) clamp omission — not applicable to Prysm

phase2_5.component_analysis: EIP-7883 iteration_count clamping (max(.,1)) is an execution-layer gas calculation concern. Prysm is a consensus client that does not implement EVM precompiles. This check must be performed against execution clients.

phase3.summary: Property cannot be proved or disproved against Prysm — no ModExp iteration_count computation exists.
phase3.invariant_proving: iteration_count >= 1 is an execution-layer invariant enforced in the ModExp precompile gas calculation. Prysm has no such code to analyze.

phase3_5.rationale: This item checks iteration_count >= 1 clamping in the ModExp precompile (EIP-7883). Zero-cost execution would be a significant DoS vulnerability, but it must be checked in execution clients (go-ethereum, etc.). Prysm is a consensus client with no EVM execution or precompile code. Definitively out of scope for OffchainLabs/prysm.
